An object of the present invention is to provide an organic thin film transistor capable of achieving high mobility, together with a method for manufacturing such an organic thin film transistor.

This object is achieved by providing a base material, a gate electrode, a gate insulating layer, an organic semiconductor layer, a source electrode, and a drain electrode. # Organic Thin Film Transistor with High Mobility and Manufacturing Method

## Objective of the Invention

The present invention aims to provide an organic thin film transistor characterized by high mobility, together with a method for manufacturing such a device. Achieving high charge carrier mobility is essential for improving the performance and efficiency of organic electronic components, and the present invention addresses this need through both its structural configuration and its fabrication process.

## Structure of the Transistor

The organic thin film transistor is constructed from several key components. It comprises a base material that serves as the foundational support for the device, upon which a gate electrode is formed. A gate insulating layer is provided to electrically separate the gate electrode from the semiconducting region. An organic semiconductor layer functions as the active layer through which charge carriers travel. In addition, the transistor includes a source electrode and a drain electrode, which enable the injection and collection of charge carriers during device operation.

## Charge Injection Layers

A distinguishing feature of the invention is the inclusion of charge injection layers. These layers are positioned between the source and drain electrodes and the layers located on their respective base material sides. The charge injection layers facilitate efficient transfer of charge carriers between the electrodes and the adjacent layers, thereby contributing to the enhanced mobility of the device.

Notably, each charge injection layer is configured with a thickness that decreases in the direction opposite to the direction in which the source and drain electrodes face each other. In other words, the layers are thickest at the region nearest the facing edges of the electrodes and taper progressively toward the outer sides. This graded thickness profile plays an important role in optimizing charge injection and overall transistor performance.

## Manufacturing Method

The method for manufacturing the organic thin film transistor involves two principal steps. First, a metal layer is scanned with a laser in order to form the source and drain electrodes. This laser-scanning process defines the electrode patterns with precision. Second, a solution is added dropwise onto the laser-scanned portion, thereby forming the charge injection layers in the desired locations.

Through this combination of laser scanning and dropwise solution deposition, the charge injection layers are formed with the characteristic tapered thickness described above, resulting in an organic thin film transistor that exhibits high mobility.

# Achieving High Mobility in Organic Thin Film Transistors Through Tapered Charge Injection Layers

## Introduction

Organic thin film transistors (OTFTs) have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation electronic applications, including flexible displays, wearable devices, and low-cost printed circuits. However, one of the persistent challenges in developing high-performance OTFTs has been achieving sufficiently high carrier mobility, which directly governs the speed and efficiency of these devices. This text addresses this fundamental challenge by introducing an innovative device structure that incorporates tapered charge injection layers, along with a novel manufacturing method to realize this design.

## The Challenge of Carrier Mobility

In conventional organic thin film transistors, the interface between the source/drain electrodes and the organic semiconductor layer plays a critical role in determining overall device performance. Poor charge injection at these interfaces creates energy barriers and contact resistance that limit the flow of carriers, ultimately reducing the achievable mobility. Overcoming these interfacial limitations has become a central focus for researchers seeking to enhance transistor efficiency.

## The Proposed Device Structure

To address these limitations, this approach introduces a device architecture featuring tapered charge injection layers strategically positioned between the source/drain electrodes and the base-side layer of the transistor. The tapered geometry of these injection layers is a key innovation, as it facilitates a more gradual and efficient transition for charge carriers moving from the metal electrodes into the semiconductor material. By reducing the abruptness of the interface and optimizing the injection pathway, this configuration minimizes contact resistance and promotes smoother carrier transport.

## Manufacturing Process

The fabrication of these tapered charge injection layers is accomplished through a two-step process. First, a metal layer is subjected to laser scanning, which precisely shapes the material and creates the desired tapered profile. This laser-based patterning allows for controlled and accurate formation of the injection layer geometry. Following the laser scanning step, a charge injection solution is applied dropwise onto the prepared surface. This deposition method ensures that the charge injection material is properly distributed and integrated into the tapered structure, completing the formation of the functional injection layers.

## Benefits and Applications

The combination of this specialized device structure and manufacturing technique yields significant improvements in transistor performance. By enabling higher carrier mobility, the tapered charge injection layers directly enhance the electrical characteristics of the organic thin film transistor. This improvement translates into faster switching speeds, greater efficiency, and superior overall functionality.

## Conclusion

In summary, this approach offers a promising solution to the longstanding challenge of achieving high mobility in organic thin film transistors. Through the introduction of tapered charge injection layers—fabricated via laser scanning of a metal layer followed by dropwise application of a charge injection solution—the device achieves enhanced carrier mobility and improved performance. These advancements hold considerable potential for advancing the capabilities of organic electronic applications, paving the way for more efficient and reliable devices in the future.

An organic thin film transistor (OTFT) device is disclosed comprising a base substrate, a semiconductor layer, and source and drain electrodes, wherein charge injection layers are disposed between the electrodes and an adjacent base material to enhance device performance. # Patent Abstract

## High-Mobility Organic Thin Film Transistor and Fabrication Method Thereof

**Abstract**

Disclosed is an organic thin film transistor (OTFT) exhibiting enhanced charge carrier mobility and a method for fabricating the same. The device comprises a substrate, a gate electrode, a dielectric layer, an organic semiconductor layer, and source/drain electrodes configured to optimize charge transport. High mobility is achieved through a synergistic combination of precision electrode formation and interfacial charge injection engineering.

In accordance with the disclosed method, the source and drain electrodes are formed by laser scanning of a conductive precursor film deposited on the substrate. A focused laser beam is scanned across the precursor layer along predefined patterns, locally sintering or ablating the material to define electrode geometries with sub-micron edge definition and reduced contact resistance. The laser scanning parameters, including beam power, scan speed, and spot size, are controlled to produce electrodes having smooth, well-defined channel edges that minimize parasitic charge trapping.

Subsequent to electrode formation, a charge injection solution is applied by controlled dropwise addition onto the electrode-semiconductor interface region. The charge injection solution comprises a dopant or interfacial modifier that, upon deposition and drying, forms a molecular interlayer reducing the injection barrier between the electrodes and the organic semiconductor. The dropwise addition enables spatially selective, quantity-controlled deposition, promoting favorable energy level alignment and increased carrier density at the contact interface.

The resulting device demonstrates substantially improved field-effect mobility, reduced contact resistance, and enhanced operational stability relative to conventionally fabricated OTFTs. The disclosed method is compatible with low-temperature, solution-processable, and large-area manufacturing, rendering it suitable for flexible electronics, display backplanes, and sensor applications.

---

*Note: This is a sample/illustrative abstract. For an actual patent filing, technical specifics (e.g., exact laser wavelengths, solution compositions, measured mobility values) should be supplied and reviewed by a qualified patent attorney.*
